cues.en: If you had to choose right now, how long would you want to live? 80?
cues.zh: 如果现在就要选，你想活多久？80岁？

cues.en: Longer?
cues.zh: 更久？

cues.en: And do you think you'll change your mind once you reach that age?
cues.zh: 你觉得到了那个年纪，你会改变主意吗？

cues.en: Fifty thousand years ago, most humans died very young.
cues.zh: 五万年前，大多数人都很年轻就死了。

cues.en: As we learned how to use the resources around us to treat ourselves, this got better and better.
cues.zh: 随着我们学会利用周围的资源来治疗自己，情况不断改善。

cues.en: Today, humans are living longer and healthier lives than ever before.
cues.zh: 如今，人类比历史上任何时候都活得更久、更健康。

cues.en: But this has an unforeseen consequence.
cues.zh: 但这带来了一个未曾预料的后果。

cues.en: We spend an ever increasing part of our lives being sick and in need of care.
cues.zh: 我们一生中患病、需要照护的时间越来越长。

cues.en: Most of us will die in a hospital bed, which is depressing enough by itself, but we also have to witness the same happening to our loved ones.
cues.zh: 我们大多数人都会在病床上死去，光是这一点就够令人沮丧了，而且我们还得亲眼看着所爱的人经历同样的过程。

cues.en: Except, maybe,
cues.zh: 不过，也许

cues.en: we can stop this forever.
cues.zh: 我们可以永远终结这一切。

cues.en: The most effective way to treat a disease is to prevent it. It saves many more lives if you stop a million people from smoking than coming up with better chemotherapies.
cues.zh: 治疗疾病最有效的方法是预防疾病。阻止一百万人吸烟，比研发更好的化疗方法能挽救更多生命。

cues.en: So why not put a halt to the cause of all disease, the process of aging?
cues.zh: 所以，为什么不彻底阻止一切疾病的根源，也就是衰老过程呢？

cues.en: In a nutshell, aging is caused by physics and not biology.
cues.zh: 简单来说，衰老是由物理学而非生物学造成的。

cues.en: Think of cars.
cues.zh: 想想汽车。

cues.en: Parts wear down from rubbing and grinding.
cues.zh: 零件会因摩擦和磨损而损坏。

cues.en: Metal rusts, filters get plugged, rubber cracks.
cues.zh: 金属会生锈，滤网会堵塞，橡胶会开裂。

cues.en: Our bodies are worn down by trillions of tiny physical processes.
cues.zh: 我们的身体也在数万亿个微小的物理过程中逐渐损耗。

cues.en: Oxygen,
cues.zh: 氧气、

cues.en: radiation from the sun, our metabolism.
cues.zh: 来自太阳的辐射，还有我们的新陈代谢。

cues.en: Our bodies have many mechanisms to repair this damage, but over time, they become less effective.
cues.zh: 我们的身体有许多修复这些损伤的机制，但随着时间推移，它们会逐渐失效。

cues.en: So our bones and muscles weaken, our skin wrinkles, our immune system gets weaker,
cues.zh: 于是我们的骨骼和肌肉变得虚弱，皮肤出现皱纹，免疫系统变弱，

cues.en: we lose our memory, and our senses diminish.
cues.zh: 我们的记忆力衰退，感官也逐渐减退。

cues.en: There's no such thing as dying of old age. We all die because one of our important parts breaks.
cues.zh: 世上根本没有所谓的“老死”。我们死亡，只是因为某个关键身体部件坏掉了。

cues.en: The older we get, the more damaged and fragile we become until one or multiple diseases take over and kill us.
cues.zh: 我们年纪越大，身体受损越严重、越脆弱，直到一种或多种疾病彻底击垮我们。

cues.en: Unnoticed by most of us, longevity research has made some unprecedented advances in the last few years. For the first time, we're starting to understand the mechanisms behind aging and how to manipulate them.
cues.zh: 在大家未曾留意的地方，长寿研究在过去几年取得了前所未有的突破。我们破天荒地开始理解衰老背后的机制，以及如何干预它们。

cues.en: Aging is neither mystical nor inevitable,
cues.zh: 衰老既不神秘，也非不可避免，

cues.en: and we might be able to stop or delay it during your lifetime.
cues.zh: 甚至在你的有生之年，我们就有可能阻止或延缓衰老。

cues.en: We'll discuss the science behind it and how scientists are trying to stop it in another video.
cues.zh: 我们会在另一期视频中讨论这背后的科学原理，以及科学家们正如何尝试阻止衰老。

cues.en: But first, if we could, should we end aging?
cues.zh: 但首先，如果我们能做到，我们真的应该终结衰老吗？

cues.en: Is this a good idea?
cues.zh: 这是个好主意吗？

cues.en: The end of aging or life extension makes many people uncomfortable.
cues.zh: 终结衰老或延长寿命，会让许多人感到不安。

cues.en: We're born, are young, become older, and then we die.
cues.zh: 我们出生，年轻，老去，然后走向死亡。

cues.en: This has been the natural order for literally all of human history, and getting old is a good thing. Right?
cues.zh: 纵观整个人类历史，这向来是自然规律，而且变老是一件好事，对吧？

cues.en: We celebrate the idea of living long enough to experience old age. We even call them the golden years.
cues.zh: 我们歌颂长寿、期待安享晚年，甚至称其为“黄金岁月”。

cues.en: But the reality is that everybody wants to become old, but nobody wants to be old.
cues.zh: 但现实是，人人都想长寿，却没人想变老。

cues.en: Think of the Greek myth of Tithonus, for example.
cues.zh: 比如想想希腊神话里的 Tithonus。

cues.en: Tithonus was the lover of the goddess Eos, and probably an amazing dude because she begged Zeus to grant him immortality
cues.zh: Tithonus 是女神 Eos 的情人，他大概极具魅力，以至于女神恳求 Zeus 赐予他永生，

cues.en: so they could spend eternity together.
cues.zh: 好让他们能永生相伴。

cues.en: But she forgot to specifically ask for eternal youth.
cues.zh: 但她唯独忘了祈求永葆青春。

cues.en: Tithurnus was granted eternal life, but he kept aging, unable to die.
cues.zh: Tithurnus 获得了永生，但他却一直在变老，无法死去。

cues.en: After a few hundred years, he was reduced to the size of a grape, babbling on senselessly forever.
cues.zh: 几百年后，他缩成了一颗葡萄大小，永远在语无伦次地呓语。

cues.en: Thousands of years ago, humans already feared never ending old age. But ending aging does not mean getting weaker and weaker. If you become too old, it's too late.
cues.zh: 几千年前，人类就已经开始害怕永无止境的衰老。但终结衰老并不意味着变得越来越虚弱。如果你已经太老，那就太迟了。

cues.en: A 90 year old who stopped aging would die anyway after a few years. Too much damage has been done to his internal machinery. There are already too many surfaces for disease to attack.
cues.zh: 一个停止衰老的 90 岁老人，几年后也依然会死去。他身体内部机制的受损太严重了，已经给疾病留下了太多的攻击面。

cues.en: Instead, the concept of life extension promises to end diseases,
cues.zh: 相反，延寿的概念承诺的是终结疾病，

cues.en: and with them, the end of a fixed maximum age.
cues.zh: 并随之打破固定的寿命上限。

cues.en: We don't know how much we could prolong our lives. We might make every human healthy to the currently accepted maximum age of around 120,
cues.zh: 我们不知道自己能把寿命延长多久。我们或许能让人人健康地活到目前公认的 120 岁左右的极限，

cues.en: or we might stop biological aging and disease indefinitely.
cues.zh: 又或者我们能无限期地遏制生物学意义上的衰老和疾病。

cues.en: Nobody knows at this point what's possible.
cues.zh: 目前没人知道究竟能做到哪一步。

cues.en: Okay. But even if we could achieve that, should we?
cues.zh: 好吧。但即便我们能做到，我们应该这么做吗？

cues.en: Well, life extension is really just another phrase for medicine.
cues.zh: 其实，延寿不过是现代医学的另一种说法罢了。

cues.en: All the doctors are doing is trying to prolong life and minimize suffering.
cues.zh: 医生所做的一切，都是为了延长生命并减轻痛苦。

cues.en: The vast majority of health care resources are spent on the consequences of aging.
cues.zh: 绝大部分医疗资源，其实都花在了应对衰老带来的后果上。

cues.en: Nearly half of your lifetime health care costs will be spent during your senior years and another third during middle age.
cues.zh: 你一生中近一半的医疗开销会花在晚年，还有三分之一花在中年。

cues.en: We are actually already trying to prolong life with our current medicine, we're just doing it very inefficiently.
cues.zh: 实际上，我们现有的医学已经在尝试延寿了，只是效率非常低下而已。

cues.en: Trying to stop aging from happening is not less natural than transplanting a heart, treating cancer with chemotherapy,
cues.zh: 试图阻止衰老发生，并不比心脏移植、用化疗治疗癌症、

cues.en: using antibiotics or vaccines.
cues.zh: 使用抗生素或疫苗更不自然。

cues.en: Nothing humans do nowadays is purely natural anymore, and we enjoy the highest standard of living ever as a consequence of that.
cues.zh: 如今人类所做的一切都不再是纯粹自然的，而正因如此，我们才享受着有史以来最高的生活水平。

cues.en: What we're doing right now is waiting until it's too late and the machine is failing.
cues.zh: 我们现在做的，是等到一切太迟、机器开始衰竭。

cues.en: And then we use the vast majority of our resources trying to fix it as well as we can while it breaks down even further.
cues.zh: 然后我们动用绝大部分资源，在它进一步崩坏时尽力去修补。

cues.en: But life extension still feels hubristic.
cues.zh: 但延长寿命仍让人觉得狂妄。

cues.en: Most people assume that they will want to die once they reach a certain age, and this might still be true.
cues.zh: 大多数人以为，自己到了某个年纪就会想死，这或许仍是真的。

cues.en: The idea of avoiding death entirely is off putting for many.
cues.zh: 完全逃避死亡的想法让许多人反感。

cues.en: The end of biological aging would not mean the end of death in any way.
cues.zh: 生物学衰老的终结，绝不意味着死亡的终结。

cues.en: It's more like a summer evening when you were a kid and your mom called you inside.
cues.zh: 它更像小时候的夏日傍晚，妈妈喊你进屋。

cues.en: You just wanted to keep playing, have a little more fun during sunset before you went to sleep. It's not about playing outside forever, just a little longer until we feel tired.
cues.zh: 你只想继续玩，在日落时分多玩一会儿再去睡觉。这不是要永远在外面玩，只是再多玩一会儿，直到我们感到累了。

cues.en: If you imagine a world without disease where you and your loved ones could live in good health for another one hundred or two hundred years, how would this change us?
cues.zh: 想象一个没有疾病的世界，你和所爱之人能健康地再活一百或两百年，这会如何改变我们？

cues.en: Would we take better care of our planet if we knew we would be around longer?
cues.zh: 如果我们知道自己能活得更久，会不会更好地照料我们的星球？

cues.en: If we could work for one hundred and fifty years, how much time would we spend figuring out what we're good at? How much more time would we spend learning?
cues.zh: 如果我们能工作一百五十年，我们会花多少时间弄清楚自己擅长什么？又会多花多少时间去学习？

cues.en: Would the intense feeling of pressure and stress many of us are feeling right now go away or get worse?
cues.zh: 我们很多人此刻感受到的强烈压力和紧张感，是会消失还是会变得更糟？

cues.en: So asking again,
cues.zh: 所以再问一次，

cues.en: if you could choose how long to live right now in good health and with your friends and family, what's your personal answer?
cues.zh: 如果你现在就能选择在身体健康、亲友相伴的情况下活多久，你个人的答案是什么？

cues.en: What would you like your future to look like?
cues.zh: 你希望你的未来是什么样子？

cues.en: But maybe you're still unconvinced.
cues.zh: 但也许你还是不认同。

cues.en: Some nagging feeling remains.
cues.zh: 总有些挥之不去的疑虑。

cues.en: That is the reaper whispering into your brain. Watch my video to hear what he says and why you shouldn't listen.
cues.zh: 那是死神在你脑中低语。看我的视频，听听他说了什么，以及为什么你不该听。

cues.en: Your eternal future may depend on it.
cues.zh: 你永恒的未来可能取决于此。

cues.en: Go watch the other part over at CGB Grey's channel. And if you're not already subscribed,
cues.zh: 去CGB Grey的频道看另一部分。如果你还没订阅，

cues.en: subscribe.
cues.zh: 就订阅吧。
